claim: Early electrophysiological brain oscillations recorded in preterm babies and newborn rodents are initially mostly driven by bottom-up sensorimotor activity.
source: Early electrophysiological brain oscillations recorded in preterm babies and newborn rodents are initially mostly driven by bottom-up sensorimotor activity and only later can detach from external inputs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general observation about early brain development, supported by the broader literature context.

claim: Early brain oscillations can later detach from external inputs.
source: Early electrophysiological brain oscillations recorded in preterm babies and newborn rodents are initially mostly driven by bottom-up sensorimotor activity and only later can detach from external inputs.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract about developmental progression.

claim: The developmental disengagement from external inputs is a hallmark of most developing brain areas, including the hippocampus.
source: This is a hallmark of most developing brain areas, including the hippocampus, which, in the adult brain, functions in integrating external inputs onto internal dynamics.
evidence: This is stated as a general principle in the abstract.

claim: The adult hippocampus functions in integrating external inputs onto internal dynamics.
source: This is a hallmark of most developing brain areas, including the hippocampus, which, in the adult brain, functions in integrating external inputs onto internal dynamics.
evidence: This describes the known function of the adult hippocampus.

claim: The developmental timeline for disengagement from external inputs remains unknown.
source: Despite its importance, the developmental timeline and circuit basis for this disengagement remain unknown.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the abstract.

claim: The circuit basis for disengagement from external inputs remains unknown.
source: Despite its importance, the developmental timeline and circuit basis for this disengagement remain unknown.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the abstract.

claim: Most CA1 pyramidal cells switch from activated to inhibited by self-generated movements at the end of the first postnatal week.
source: Indeed, most CA1 pyramidal cells switch from activated to inhibited by self-generated movements at the end of the first postnatal week, whereas the majority of GABAergic neurons remain positively modulated throughout this period.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: The majority of GABAergic neurons remain positively modulated by self-generated movements throughout the first postnatal week and into the second week.
source: Indeed, most CA1 pyramidal cells switch from activated to inhibited by self-generated movements at the end of the first postnatal week, whereas the majority of GABAergic neurons remain positively modulated throughout this period.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: The switch in CA1 pyramidal cell response to movement occurs within 2 days.
source: This rapid switch occurs within 2 days and follows the rapid anatomical and functional surge of local somatic GABAergic innervation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data showing the transition between P8 and P10.

claim: The switch in CA1 pyramidal cell response follows the rapid anatomical and functional surge of local somatic GABAergic innervation.
source: This rapid switch occurs within 2 days and follows the rapid anatomical and functional surge of local somatic GABAergic innervation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by anatomical data in Figure 4.

claim: The observed change in dynamics is consistent with a two-population model undergoing a strengthening of inhibition.
source: The observed change in dynamics is consistent with a two-population model undergoing a strengthening of inhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by modeling results in Figure 5.

claim: The abrupt developmental transition inaugurates the emergence of internal hippocampal dynamics.
source: We propose that this abrupt developmental transition inaugurates the emergence of internal hippocampal dynamics.
evidence: This is the main interpretive conclusion proposed in the abstract.

claim: The adult hippocampus serves multiple cognitive functions, including navigation and memory.
source: The adult hippocampus serves multiple cognitive functions, including navigation and memory.
evidence: This is established knowledge stated in the introduction.

claim: Hippocampal cognitive functions rely on the ability to integrate external inputs onto internally generated dynamics.
source: These functions rely on the ability of hippocampal circuits to integrate external inputs conveying multisensory, proprioceptive, contextual, and emotional information onto internally generated dynamics.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established understanding.

claim: The capacity to produce internally coordinated neuronal activity detached from environmental inputs is central to hippocampal cognitive functions such as planning and memory.
source: Therefore, the capacity to produce internally coordinated neuronal activity detached from environmental inputs is central to the cognitive functions of the hippocampus such as planning and memory (Buzsáki, 2015; Buzsáki and Moser, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The developing hippocampus is mainly driven by bottom-up external environmental and body-derived signals.
source: In contrast to the adult situation, the developing hippocampus, like many developing cortical structures, is mainly driven by bottom-up external environmental and body-derived signals, including motor twitches generated in the spinal cord and/or the brainstem (Dooley et al., 2020; Inácio et al., 2016; Karlsson et al., 2006; Mohns and Blumberg, 2010; Del Rio-Bermudez et al., 2020; Valeeva et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple supporting citations.

claim: Motor twitches in the developing hippocampus are generated in the spinal cord and/or the brainstem.
source: In contrast to the adult situation, the developing hippocampus, like many developing cortical structures, is mainly driven by bottom-up external environmental and body-derived signals, including motor twitches generated in the spinal cord and/or the brainstem (Dooley et al., 2020; Inácio et al., 2016; Karlsson et al., 2006; Mohns and Blumberg, 2010; Del Rio-Bermudez et al., 2020; Valeeva et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Early sharp waves are produced by motor twitches and conveyed by inputs from the entorhinal cortex.
source: These produce early sharp waves (eSW) conveyed by inputs from the entorhinal cortex (Valeeva et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: The emergence of self-organized sequences without reliance on external cues in the form of sharp wave ripples is only observed after the end of the second postnatal week.
source: The emergence of self-organized sequences without reliance on external cues in the form of sharp wave ripples (SWRs) is only observed after the end of the second postnatal week and sequential reactivations even a week later (Farooq and Dragoi, 2019; Muessig et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Sequential reactivations are observed a week after the emergence of sharp wave ripples.
source: The emergence of self-organized sequences without reliance on external cues in the form of sharp wave ripples (SWRs) is only observed after the end of the second postnatal week and sequential reactivations even a week later (Farooq and Dragoi, 2019; Muessig et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Early hippocampal activity is first externally driven while the emergence of internal dynamics is protracted.
source: Therefore, early hippocampal activity as measured with electrophysiological recordings is first externally driven while the emergence of internal dynamics is protracted.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the introduction based on cited literature.

claim: The timing and circuit mechanisms of the switch between motion-guided and internally produced hippocampal dynamics remain unknown.
source: The timing and the circuit mechanisms of the switch between motion-guided and internally produced hippocampal dynamics remain unknown.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the introduction.

claim: The switch between motion-guided and internally produced hippocampal dynamics has been proposed to rely on the maturation of CA3 and extrinsic hippocampal inputs.
source: They have been proposed to rely on the maturation of CA3 and extrinsic hippocampal inputs; however, a possible role of local connectivity, in particular, recurrent somatic inhibition, cannot be excluded (Cossart and Khazipov, 2022).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: A possible role of local connectivity, in particular recurrent somatic inhibition, in the switch between motion-guided and internally produced hippocampal dynamics cannot be excluded.
source: They have been proposed to rely on the maturation of CA3 and extrinsic hippocampal inputs; however, a possible role of local connectivity, in particular, recurrent somatic inhibition, cannot be excluded (Cossart and Khazipov, 2022).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: Self-organized internal neuronal network dynamics require feedback connections to produce an emergent state of activity independently from incoming input.
source: First, both theoretical and experimental work suggest that self-organized internal neuronal network dynamics require feedback connections to produce an emergent state of activity independently from the incoming input (Hopfield and Tank, 2005; Hopfield, 1982; Yuste, 2015).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Feedback circuits in CA1 are mainly GABAergic, given the scarcity of recurrent glutamatergic connections.
source: Feedback circuits are mainly GABAergic in CA1 (but not necessarily inhibitory), given the scarcity of recurrent glutamatergic connections in that hippocampal subregion (Bezaire and Soltesz, 2013).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: GABAergic interneurons, in particular perisomatic subtypes, shape the spatial and temporal organization of internal CA1 dynamics.
source: Second, GABAergic interneurons, in particular, the perisomatic subtypes, are long known to shape the spatial and temporal organization of internal CA1 dynamics (Buzsáki, 2015; Lee et al., 2014; Soltesz and Losonczy, 2018; Valero et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: GABAergic perisomatic cells display a delayed maturation profile both at structural and functional levels.
source: However, GABAergic perisomatic cells display a delayed maturation profile both at structural (Jiang et al., 2001; Marty et al., 2002; Morozov and Freund, 2003; Tyzio et al., 1999) and functional levels (Ben-Ari, 2002; Doischer et al., 2008; Jiang et al., 2001; Khazipov et al., 2004; Marty et al., 2002; Morozov and Freund, 2003; Murata and Colonnese, 2020; Tyzio et al., 1999), and the precise developmental timeline for their postnatal development remains unknown, partly due to the difficulty in labeling them (Donato et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with multiple supporting citations.

claim: The precise developmental timeline for postnatal development of GABAergic perisomatic cells remains unknown, partly due to the difficulty in labeling them.
source: However, GABAergic perisomatic cells display a delayed maturation profile both at structural (Jiang et al., 2001; Marty et al., 2002; Morozov and Freund, 2003; Tyzio et al., 1999) and functional levels (Ben-Ari, 2002; Doischer et al., 2008; Jiang et al., 2001; Khazipov et al., 2004; Marty et al., 2002; Morozov and Freund, 2003; Murata and Colonnese, 2020; Tyzio et al., 1999), and the precise developmental timeline for their postnatal development remains unknown, partly due to the difficulty in labeling them (Donato et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap with a supporting citation.

claim: Pups were injected with AAV1-hSyn-GCaMP6s.WPRE.SV40 virus in the brain lateral ventricle on the day of birth (P0).
source: In order to induce stable and early expression of the calcium indicator protein GCaMP6s, pups were injected with the AAV1-hSyn-GCaMP6s.WPRE.SV40 virus in the brain lateral ventricle on the day of birth (P0, Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used, shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The hippocampal CA1 region of non-anesthetized pups was imaged through a window implant placed 5 to 12 days after injection.
source: Five to twelve days after injection, the hippocampal CA1 region of non-anesthetized pups was imaged through a window implant placed on the same day (Figure 1A, see 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This describes the experimental method, shown in Figure 1A.

claim: P5-6 mice spent 74% (±6) of their time in active sleep after cranial window surgery and EMG electrode implantation.
source: We found that mice spent 74% (±6) of their time in active sleep (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), which is comparable to previous reports (Jouvet-Mounier et al., 1970).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement reported with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The time spent in active sleep by P5-6 mice after surgery is comparable to previous reports.
source: We found that mice spent 74% (±6) of their time in active sleep (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), which is comparable to previous reports (Jouvet-Mounier et al., 1970).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: The window implant did not alter the characteristic sleep-wake cycle behavior in early postnatal stages.
source: This indicates that the window implant did not alter this characteristic of behavior in early postnatal stages.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the sleep-wake data.

claim: The acute window implant did not significantly alter electrophysiological network patterns.
source: In the same way, the acute window implant did not significantly alter electrophysiological network patterns.
evidence: This is stated based on electrophysiological measurements.

claim: Early sharp waves were measured using in vivo bilateral silicon probes recordings in P6-8 and P11 pups expressing GCaMP6s.
source: These were measured using in vivo bilateral silicon probes recordings of eSW (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, see 'Discussion') in P6–8 (n = 4) and P11 (n = 2) pups expressing GCaMP6s with a frequency of 2.6 eSW/min (25% 1.15 eSW/min and 75% 4.16 eSW/min) for the ipsilateral side and 3.49 eSW/min (25% 1.96 eSW/min and 75% 5.1 eSW/min, p-value=0.39) for the contralateral side (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This reports electrophysiological measurements with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The frequency of early sharp waves was 2.6 eSW/min for the ipsilateral side and 3.49 eSW/min for the contralateral side.
source: These were measured using in vivo bilateral silicon probes recordings of eSW (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, see 'Discussion') in P6–8 (n = 4) and P11 (n = 2) pups expressing GCaMP6s with a frequency of 2.6 eSW/min (25% 1.15 eSW/min and 75% 4.16 eSW/min) for the ipsilateral side and 3.49 eSW/min (25% 1.96 eSW/min and 75% 5.1 eSW/min, p-value=0.39) for the contralateral side (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This reports quantitative electrophysiological measurements.

claim: There was a slight but nonsignificant reduction in eSW frequency recorded from the ipsilateral hemisphere.
source: This slight but nonsignificant reduction in eSW frequency recorded from the ipsilateral hemisphere was similarly reported in a previous study using the same surgical approach (see 'Discussion', Graf et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: eSW synchronization between hemispheres was preserved but with a 12 ms delay.
source: eSW synchronization between hemispheres was preserved (Valeeva et al., 2019b) but with a 12 ms delay between the two hemispheres (peak at 0.087 ± 0.027 s, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), possibly explained by a slight drop in local temperature due to the chamber placement as described previously (Reig et al., 2010).
evidence: This reports a quantitative measurement with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and supporting citations.

claim: A peak in the theta range was observed in P11 mouse pups in both hemispheres.
source: Finally, we checked for the presence of other types of oscillations in both hemispheres and observed a peak in the theta range in the P11 mouse pups in both hemispheres (ipsi: peak at 4.3 Hz of amplitude 3.6 × 10–3 ± 1.2 × 10–3 mV2/Hz; contra: peak at 4.1 Hz of amplitude 2 × 10–3 ± 3 × 10–4 mV2/Hz (jackknife standard deviation), Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This reports a quantitative measurement with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: A slight increase in the peak power of most electrophysiological network oscillations (below 20 Hz) was observed.
source: In general, a slight increase in the peak power of most electrophysiological network oscillations (below 20 Hz) was observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This reports an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The presence of the window implant minimally disrupted the electrophysiological network patterns and sleep-wake cycle of developing rodents during the early postnatal period.
source: Altogether, we can conclude that the presence of the window implant minimally disrupted the electrophysiological network patterns and sleep–wake cycle of developing rodents during that early postnatal period.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the electrophysiological and behavioral data.

claim: 62 imaging sessions were performed on 35 mouse pups aged between 5 and 12 days, yielding a total of 33,412 cells.
source: Thus, we pursued the description of early multineuron CA1 dynamics using calcium imaging (62 imaging sessions, 35 mouse pups aged between 5 and 12 days, yielding a total of 33,412 cells, see Supplementary file 1 for details of each session and their inclusion in the figures).
evidence: This reports the sample size for the calcium imaging experiments.

claim: In P5-6 mouse pups, more than half of the detected calcium transients occurred within synchronous calcium events (SCEs).
source: In P5–6 mouse pups, more than half of the detected calcium transients occurred within SCEs (P5: median value 55% N = 4, n = 8; P6: median value 55% N = 3, n = 5; N: mice, n: imaging sessions, Figure 1B).
evidence: This reports a quantitative measurement with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Activity became progressively continuous as evidenced by the linear decrease in the proportion of calcium transients occurring during SCEs (r2 = 0.78, p<0.0001).
source: Activity then became progressively continuous as evidenced by the linear decrease in the proportion of calcium transients occurring during SCEs (r2 = 0.78, p<0.0001) to finally reach 33% in P12 mouse pups (P12: N = 5, n = 8, Figure 1B).
evidence: This reports a quantitative analysis with statistical values and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The proportion of calcium transients occurring during SCEs reached 33% in P12 mouse pups.
source: Activity then became progressively continuous as evidenced by the linear decrease in the proportion of calcium transients occurring during SCEs (r2 = 0.78, p<0.0001) to finally reach 33% in P12 mouse pups (P12: N = 5, n = 8, Figure 1B).
evidence: This reports a quantitative measurement with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: A nonlinear evolution in cell activation frequency was observed with a local minimum around P10 (r2 = 0.30).
source: Reminiscent of a transient period of 'neural quiescence' at the beginning of the second postnatal week (Domínguez et al., 2021), we observed a nonlinear evolution in the cell activation frequency with a local minimum around P10 (r2 = 0.30, Figure 1C).
evidence: This reports a quantitative analysis with reference to Figure 1C and a supporting citation.

claim: CA1 dynamics progressively evolve from discontinuous to continuous during the first two postnatal weeks.
source: We conclude that CA1 dynamics progressively evolve from discontinuous to continuous during the first two postnatal weeks, in agreement with previous electrophysiological studies (Cossart and Khazipov, 2022; Mohns and Blumberg, 2008; Valeeva et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion with supporting citations.

claim: Both spontaneous ipsilateral and contralateral limb movements were followed by an increase in CA1 activity.
source: Both spontaneous limb movements were followed by an increase in CA1 activity (peak ipsi = 3.6%, peak contra = 2.8%, chance level 3.4%, Figure 1—figure supplement 1E), showing that the surgery was not preventing the hippocampal response to contralateral limb movements.
evidence: This reports quantitative measurements with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Contralateral limb movements recruited a slightly lower fraction of active cells than ipsilateral movements.
source: Still, contralateral limb movements recruited a slightly lower fraction of active cells (see 'Discussion').
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: In mouse pups younger than P9, movements were followed by a significant increase in the percentage of active cells exceeding the chance level.
source: In mouse pups younger than P9, movements were followed by a significant increase in the percentage of active cells exceeding the chance level (Figure 2A; P5–8 median above chance level, Videos 1–3) and an increase in the average DF/F fluorescence signal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This reports a finding with reference to Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: After P9, movements were followed by a significant decrease in activity below chance level.
source: In contrast, after P9, movements were followed by a significant decrease in activity below chance level (Figure 2A, P10–12 median below chance level, Videos 4–6) and a decreased DF/F fluorescence signal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This reports a finding with reference to Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: When combining all mouse pups and considering separately twitches and complex movements, the two movement types did not significantly differ in their impact on CA1 activity.
source: However, when combining all mouse pups, and considering separately twitches (occurring during REM/active sleep) and complex movements (occurring during wakefulness), based on video recordings, we found that the two movement types did not significantly differ in their impact on CA1 activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This reports a finding with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The median post-movement activity progressively decreased from P5 to P9.
source: The median post-movement activity progressively decreased from P5 to P9 (mean difference between consecutive age groups of 3.1 ± 0.7%) until it suddenly dropped at P10 (–13.5% between P9 and P10) and stabilized until P12.
evidence: This reports a quantitative analysis of the data.

claim: There was a sudden drop in median post-movement activity at P10 (–13.5% between P9 and P10).
source: The median post-movement activity progressively decreased from P5 to P9 (mean difference between consecutive age groups of 3.1 ± 0.7%) until it suddenly dropped at P10 (–13.5% between P9 and P10) and stabilized until P12.
evidence: This reports a quantitative measurement.

claim: P9 marked the transition in the relationship between movement and CA1 activity.
source: P9 marked the transition in the relationship between movement and CA1 activity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the data analysis.

claim: The median post-movement activity exceeded 50% from P5 to P8.
source: Indeed, the median post-movement activity exceeded 50% from P5 to P8 (P5: 71%; P6: 65%; P7: 60%; P8: 56%).
evidence: This reports quantitative measurements.

claim: After P9, the median post-movement activity was lower than 50%.
source: After P9, the median post-movement activity was lower than 50% (P10: 39%; P11: 35%; P12: 40%), thus revealing the inhibitory action of movement on activity.
evidence: This reports quantitative measurements.

claim: The proportion of 'inhibiting' movements was stable before P9.
source: The proportion of 'inhibiting' movements was stable before P9 (P5: 11%; P6: 16%; P7: 10%, P8: 15%).
evidence: This reports quantitative measurements.

claim: Approximately half of the movements were followed by an inhibition of CA1 activity in P10-12 mice.
source: Again, P9 marks a transition since we observed that approximately half of the movements were followed by an inhibition of CA1 activity in P10–12 mice (P10: 55%; P11: 58%; P12: 48%).
evidence: This reports quantitative measurements.

claim: The proportion of 'inhibiting' movements varies with age as a sigmoid function with P9 being the transition time point (V50 = 9.015, r2 = 0.75).
source: The proportion of 'inhibiting' movements varies with age as a sigmoid function with P9 being the transition time point (V50 = 9.015, r2 = 0.75).
evidence: This reports a quantitative analysis with statistical values.

claim: The fraction of neurons significantly associated with immobility increased with age, following a sigmoidal function (sigmoid fit V50 = 9.022, r2 = 0.55).
source: In line with the emergence of movement-induced inhibition, the fraction of neurons significantly associated with immobility also increased with age, also following a sigmoidal function (Figure 2D, sigmoid fit V50 = 9.022, r2 = 0.55).
evidence: This reports a quantitative analysis with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: The end of the first postnatal week marks a transition in the evolution of CA1 dynamics, with both a decorrelation and a 'detachment' of neuronal activity from spontaneous motor activity.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that the end of the first postnatal week marks a transition in the evolution of CA1 dynamics, with both a decorrelation and a 'detachment' of neuronal activity from spontaneous motor activity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the data.

claim: GABAergic neurons were identified with the expression of a red reporter (tdTomato) in GAD1Cre/+ pups virally infected with AAV9-FLEX-CAG-tdTomato and AAV1.hSyn.GCaMP6s.
source: To this aim, we identified GABAergic neurons with the expression of a red reporter (tdTomato) in GAD1Cre/+ pups virally infected with AAV9-FLEX-CAG-tdTomato and AAV1.hSyn.GCaMP6s (Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental method with reference to figures.

claim: A cell classifier was trained to infer interneurons in the absence of any reporter with 91% precision.
source: In addition, we used these imaging experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, top row) to train a cell classifier inferring interneurons in the absence of any reporter (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, bottom row). This classifier was able to infer interneurons with 91% precision (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C; Denis et al., 2020).
evidence: This reports the performance of the classifier with reference to figures and a citation.

claim: Both pyramidal cells and interneurons were activated during movement in pups aged less than P9.
source: As illustrated in a representative raster plot from a P5 mouse, both pyramidal cells (black) and interneurons (red) were activated during movement (vertical gray lines, Figure 3A). This was confirmed when computing the PMTH for pups aged less than P9, with the activation of the two neuronal populations after movement exceeding chance level (P5–8: N = 17, n = 33, pyramidal cells: baseline value = 0.51%, peak value = 2.1%, interneurons: baseline value = 2.1%, peak value 7.9%, N: number of mice, n: number of imaging sessions, Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This reports findings with reference to Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Pups older than P9 showed a significant reduction (below chance level) in the proportion of active pyramidal cells following movement.
source: In line with the above results (Figure 2A), pups older than P9 showed a significant reduction (below chance level) in the proportion of active pyramidal cells following movement (Figure 3B P10–12: N = 7, n = 9, baseline value = 1.3%, trough value = 0.4%).
evidence: This reports findings with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Interneurons remained significantly activated following movement even past P9.
source: In contrast, interneurons remained significantly activated following movement even past P9 (P10–12: N = 7, n = 9, baseline value = 3.9%, peak value = 10%, Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This reports findings with reference to Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The link between movement and activity evolves differentially toward the start of the second postnatal week when comparing pyramidal neurons and GABAergic interneurons.
source: We conclude that the link between movement and activity evolves differentially toward the start of the second postnatal week when comparing pyramidal neurons and GABAergic interneurons, the former being inhibited or detached from movements while the latter remaining activated.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the data.

claim: Pyramidal neurons could be directly inhibited by local interneurons after the first postnatal week, following a functional maturation of GABAergic outputs onto principal cells.
source: This suggests that pyramidal neurons could be directly inhibited by local interneurons after the first postnatal week, following a functional maturation of GABAergic outputs onto principal cells.
evidence: This is a proposed interpretation of the findings.

claim: Both GAD1Cre/+ and EmxCre/+ pups received mainly external inputs from the entorhinal cortex, medial septum, and contralateral CA3 area.
source: In agreement with previous studies (Supèr and Soriano, 1994), we found that GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons in the dorsal hippocampus received mainly external inputs from the entorhinal cortex, medial septum, and contralateral CA3 area (retrogradely labeled cells in these regions were found in four out of four GAD1Cre/+ pups and three out of three EmxCre/+ pups, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This reports findings from retrograde tracing experiments with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 3 and a citation.

claim: No major switch in the nature of the extra-hippocampal inputs impinging onto local CA1 neurons was revealed between early and late groups.
source: Thus, we could not reveal any major switch in the nature of the extra-hippocampal inputs impinging onto local CA1 neurons.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the retrograde tracing experiments.

claim: Between P3 and P7, PV innervation remained stable (median values: P3: 0.34%; P5: 0.57%; P7: 0.49%).
source: Using a custom-made Fiji plugin (RINGO, see 'Materials and methods'), we quantified the surface of the pyramidal cell layer covered by Syt2 labeling at different stages and found that between P3 and P7, PV innervation remained stable (median values: P3: 0.34%; P5: 0.57%; P7: 0.49%, three mice per group, Figure 4B).
evidence: This reports quantitative measurements with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: After P9, an increase in the density of Syt2-positive labeling was observed (P9: 1.03%; P11: 1.48%).
source: However, after P9, an increase in the density of positive labeling was observed (P9: 1.03%; P11: 1.48%, three mice per group, Figure 4B).
evidence: This reports quantitative measurements with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: The Syt2 labeling results are consistent with previous work.
source: These results are consistent with previous work (Jiang et al., 2001; Marty et al., 2002), as well as with our tdTomato labeling (Figure 3A and B) and GCaMP imaging (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Video 7).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations and references to figures.

claim: An increase in the fluorescent signal from GABAergic axonal branches was observed following movement at P9-10.
source: As expected (see Figure 3B), an increase in the fluorescent signal from GABAergic axonal branches was observed following movement (P9–10: n = 3 mice, Figure 4D).
evidence: This reports findings with reference to Figure 4D.

claim: The emergence of functional perisomatic GABAergic activity could contribute to the reduction in activity observed after movement during the second postnatal week in pyramidal neurons.
source: As a result, we reasoned that the emergence of functional perisomatic GABAergic activity could contribute to the reduction in activity observed after movement during the second postnatal week in pyramidal neurons.
evidence: This is a proposed interpretation of the findings.

claim: Increasing the number of perisomatic inhibitory connections can account for the experimentally observed decrease in responses to movement-like feedforward inputs.
source: Using a rate model and a leaky integrate and fire (LIF) model, we show that increasing the number of perisomatic inhibitory connections can account for the experimentally observed decrease in responses to movement-like feedforward inputs (Figure 5B).
evidence: This reports findings from computational modeling with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: When inhibition is weak, the average activity of pyramidal neurons increases at the onset of a given twitch and quickly relaxes to baseline.
source: When inhibition is weak, the average activity of the pyramidal neurons increases at the onset of a given twitch. Then, it quickly relaxes to the baseline with a timescale that follows the synaptic time constant (Figure 5B, left panel).
evidence: This reports findings from computational modeling with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: In the presence of strong inhibition, there is a reduction in response to movement inputs and network activity relaxes to baseline with an undershoot.
source: In the presence of strong inhibition, there is a reduction in response to movement inputs. In addition, due to strong feedback inhibition following the movement responses, network activity relaxes to the baseline with an undershoot (Figure 5B, right panel), recapitulating the experimental findings (see Figure 2A).
evidence: This reports findings from computational modeling with reference to Figure 5B and Figure 2A.

claim: For P9-12, a rapid drop in the correlation at positive time points was observed in cross-correlograms between interneurons and pyramidal cells, suggesting a feedforward inhibition of principal cells' activity.
source: For P9–12, we observed a rapid drop in the correlation at positive time points, suggesting a feedforward inhibition of principal cells' activity.
evidence: This reports findings from cross-correlation analysis.

claim: For P5-8, the cross-correlogram was symmetric and centered at zero.
source: Such drop was absent for P5–8, where the cross-correlogram was symmetric and centered at zero.
evidence: This reports findings from cross-correlation analysis.

claim: Both the rate and LIF models displayed similar activity correlograms as the experimental data.
source: Both the rate and LIF models displayed similar activity correlograms as the experimental data, with an undershoot in the presence of strong inhibitory feedback for positive time points (Figure 5C, middle and right panels).
evidence: This reports findings from computational modeling with reference to Figure 5C.

claim: The consistency of the models with the experimental cross-correlograms shows that the observed network dynamics most likely result from recurrent perisomatic inhibition rather than a feedforward drive from upstream areas.
source: The consistency of our models with the experimental cross-correlograms, which were computed from the activity recorded during periods of immobility, further shows that the observed network dynamics and, in particular, the correlation undershoots most likely result from recurrent perisomatic inhibition rather than a feedforward drive from upstream areas.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the modeling results.

claim: In the model, the maturation of perisomatic inhibition alone was sufficient to support a switch in network dynamics.
source: Therefore, in our model, the maturation of perisomatic inhibition alone was sufficient to support a switch in network dynamics.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the computational modeling.

claim: Until P7-9, spontaneous movements are followed by a significant peak in calcium events in the CA1 principal cell layer and most neuronal activity occurs during SCEs.
source: We found that, until P7–9, spontaneous movements are followed by a significant peak in calcium events in the CA1 principal cell layer and that most neuronal activity occurs during SCEs.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the Discussion based on the results.

claim: Part of the overlying cortex, including the primary sensory cortex, was removed to grant optical access to the hippocampus.
source: Of note, it is important to keep in mind that part of the overlying cortex, including the primary sensory cortex, was removed to grant optical access to the hippocampus.
evidence: This describes a methodological consideration.

claim: The surgical procedure may damage incoming axons from the temporoammonic track linking the entorhinal cortex to the hippocampus.
source: This region may contribute to relaying the sensory feedback from the twitches to the hippocampus (Khazipov and Milh, 2018; Valeeva et al., 2019a). The surgical procedure may thus damage incoming axons from the temporoammonic track linking the entorhinal cortex to the hippocampus.
evidence: This is stated as a potential limitation with supporting citations.

claim: The CA1 response to movements from the contralateral limbs was slightly reduced.
source: Accordingly, we observed (1) that the CA1 response to movements from the contralateral limbs was slightly reduced, (2) the eSW frequency in the ipsilateral hemisphere was slightly diminished, and (3) there was a small increase in the power spectra of network oscillations below 20 Hz.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: The eSW frequency in the ipsilateral hemisphere was slightly diminished.
source: Accordingly, we observed (1) that the CA1 response to movements from the contralateral limbs was slightly reduced, (2) the eSW frequency in the ipsilateral hemisphere was slightly diminished, and (3) there was a small increase in the power spectra of network oscillations below 20 Hz.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: There was a small increase in the power spectra of network oscillations below 20 Hz.
source: Accordingly, we observed (1) that the CA1 response to movements from the contralateral limbs was slightly reduced, (2) the eSW frequency in the ipsilateral hemisphere was slightly diminished, and (3) there was a small increase in the power spectra of network oscillations below 20 Hz.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: In one mouse pup, both REM and wake-associated movements were followed by an activation of CA1 neurons, with the latter triggering a smaller response.
source: In one mouse pup, we directly combined two-photon imaging with EMG recordings to better define brain states and confirmed that both REM and wake-associated movements were followed by an activation of CA1 neurons, with the latter triggering a smaller response.
evidence: This reports a finding from a specific experiment.

claim: Between P8 and P10, a significant decrease in the fraction of coactive principal cells following movement was observed.
source: Passed the end of the first postnatal week, between P8 and P10, a significant decrease in the fraction of coactive principal cells following movement was observed (while interneurons remained mostly activated by movement).
evidence: This is a summary statement in the Discussion based on the results.

claim: This change in the polarity of principal cells' response to movements is quite abrupt as it happens within less than 2 days (between P8 and 10).
source: This change in the polarity of principal cells' response to movements is quite abrupt as it happens within less than 2 days (between P8 and 10).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the data.

claim: A small increase in the fraction of active cells can be observed approximately 1 s before the onset of movement in P12 pups.
source: Of note, a small increase in the fraction of active cells can be observed approximately 1 s before the onset of movement in P12 pups, indicating that activity would start building up in CA1 prior to movement.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: Anticipatory cell firing prior to locomotion has been previously reported in the adult cortex.
source: Anticipatory cell firing prior to locomotion has been previously reported in the adult cortex (e.g., see Vinck et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: The 'internalization' of hippocampal dynamics is reminiscent of similar phenomena observed in other cortical areas, such as the barrel cortex.
source: This 'internalization' of hippocampal dynamics is reminiscent of similar phenomena observed in other cortical areas, such as the barrel cortex where whisker stimulation induces a reduction in the size of cell assemblies following P9 while the same stimulation widens cell assembly size a few days before (Modol et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: The change in CA1 dynamics occurring at the end of the first postnatal week most likely relies on structural changes in local CA1 circuits rather than rewiring of the long-range extra-hippocampal connectivity.
source: Our results demonstrate that the change in CA1 dynamics occurring at the end of the first postnatal week most likely relies on structural changes in local CA1 circuits rather than rewiring of the long-range extra-hippocampal connectivity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion in the Discussion based on the results.

claim: The two main structures directly transmitting sensorimotor information to the dorsal CA1 are the entorhinal cortex and septum.
source: The two main structures directly transmitting sensorimotor information to the dorsal CA1 are the entorhinal cortex and septum.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion.

claim: The entorhinal cortex processes multisensory information from all sensory cortices and was shown to be activated by spontaneous twitches prior to CA1.
source: The former processes multisensory information from all sensory cortices (visual, auditory, olfactory, somatosensory), including movement-related sensory feedback (Rio-Bermudez and Blumberg, 2022), and was shown to be activated by spontaneous twitches prior to CA1 (Mohns and Blumberg, 2010; Del Rio-Bermudez et al., 2020; Valeeva et al., 2019a)
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: The septum is more likely to be involved in transmitting internal information and unexpected environmental stimuli.
source: while the latter is more likely to be involved in transmitting internal information (Fuhrmann et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2015), as well as unexpected environmental stimuli (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Retrograde-tracing experiments did not reveal any direct connection between the CA1 cells and the brainstem at the early ages analyzed.
source: However, our retrograde-tracing experiments did not reveal any direct connection between the CA1 cells and the brainstem at the early ages analyzed here.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the experiments.

claim: Both CA1 interneurons and principal cells receive inputs from the septum and entorhinal cortex before the time of the switch (i.e. P9) and there was no major qualitative change of inputs after.
source: In addition, we found that both CA1 interneurons and principal cells receive inputs from the septum and entorhinal cortex before the time of the switch (i.e. P9) and that there was no major qualitative change of inputs after, as expected from previous work (Supèr and Soriano, 1994).
evidence: This is stated as a finding with a supporting citation.

claim: Schaffer collaterals are known to reach CA1 roughly around the end of the first postnatal week.
source: Indeed, Schaffer collaterals are known to reach CA1 roughly around the end of the first postnatal week (Durand et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: Roughly at the time of the switch, the emergence of SWRs is observed.
source: In addition, roughly at the time of the switch, we do see the emergence of SWRs (Buhl and Buzsáki, 2005), a pattern strongly relying on CA3 inputs and perisomatic GABAergic transmission.
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: Among the external inputs onto CA1, the entorhinal cortex and CA3 were both shown to exert a mild influence on the organization of intrinsic CA1 dynamics.
source: Interestingly, among the external inputs onto CA1 described above, the entorhinal cortex and CA3 were both shown to exert a mild influence on the organization of intrinsic CA1 dynamics, possibly pointing at a critical role of local interneurons in this process (Zutshi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: The disengagement from movement of CA1 dynamics can be fully explained by the observed rise in anatomical and functional connectivity from perisomatic GABAergic cells onto pyramidal cells at the onset of the second postnatal week.
source: As indicated by our computational model, the disengagement from movement of CA1 dynamics can be fully explained by the observed rise in anatomical (Syt2 labeling) and functional (axonal GCaMP imaging) connectivity from perisomatic GABAergic cells onto pyramidal cells at the onset of the second postnatal week.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion in the Discussion based on the modeling and experimental results.

claim: Early anatomical studies had indicated that an increase in somatic GABAergic inhibition occurred in CA1 during the first postnatal week.
source: Early anatomical studies had already indicated that an increase in somatic GABAergic inhibition, including from CCK-basket cells, occurred in CA1 during the first postnatal week (Gour et al., 2021; Danglot et al., 2006; Jiang et al., 2001; Marty et al., 2002; Morozov and Freund, 2003).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: The rise in somatic GABAergic inhibition was expected to be more progressive and not as abrupt as observed here as it happened within 2 days.
source: However, this rise was expected to be more progressive and not as abrupt as observed here as it happened within 2 days.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with previous expectations.

claim: A similar rise of somatic GABAergic axonal coverage occurs in the barrel cortex at the same time.
source: Interestingly, a similar rise of somatic GABAergic axonal coverage occurs in the barrel cortex at the same time.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with other brain regions.

claim: Recent connectomic mapping using 3D electron microscopy in the barrel cortex revealed that the preferential targeting of cell bodies by GABAergic synapses increased almost threefold between postnatal days 7 and 9.
source: Indeed, recent connectomic mapping using 3D electron microscopy in that region revealed that the preferential targeting of cell bodies by GABAergic synapses increased almost threefold between postnatal days 7 and 9 (Gour et al., 2021), whereas two-photon imaging of putative GABAergic somatic axons in the same region revealed broader domains of co-activation (Modol et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Many principal cells are inhibited by movement while most imaged GABAergic cells remained activated during the second postnatal week.
source: We found that many principal cells are inhibited by movement while most imaged GABAergic cells remained activated during the second postnatal week.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the Discussion based on the results.

claim: This indirectly suggests a net inhibitory effect of GABAergic transmission after the first postnatal week.
source: This therefore indirectly suggests a net inhibitory effect of GABAergic transmission after the first postnatal week.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings.

claim: The shift from excitatory to inhibitory synaptic transmission was reported to occur earlier in the hippocampus in vivo.
source: This is expected since the shift from excitatory to inhibitory synaptic transmission was reported to occur earlier in the hippocampus in vivo (Murata and Colonnese, 2020).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: The lack of somatic GABAergic inputs before P7 indicates that the early excitatory GABAergic drive in CA1 circuits likely originates from nonsomatic GABAergic interneurons.
source: On a side note, the lack of somatic GABAergic inputs before P7 indicates that the early excitatory GABAergic drive in CA1 circuits likely originates from nonsomatic GABAergic interneurons, which include long-range, dendrite-targeting or interneuron-specific interneurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the findings.

claim: A similar strengthening of feedback inhibition has previously been observed in the developing somatosensory cortex.
source: A similar strengthening of feedback inhibition has previously been observed in the developing somatosensory cortex (Anastasiades and Butt, 2012).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: The inhibition of activity following movement is likely to be occurring during a transient developmental period.
source: The inhibition of activity following movement is likely to be occurring during a transient developmental period.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation.

claim: In the adult, both interneurons and principal cells usually increase their activity as the animal moves.
source: Indeed, in the adult, both interneurons and principal cells usually increase their activity as the animal moves (Fuhrmann et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: The switch observed here opens another developmental time window that probably closes with the emergence of perineuronal nets and cell activation sequences at the end of the third developmental week.
source: Therefore, the switch observed here opens another developmental time window that probably closes with the emergence of perineuronal nets and cell activation sequences at the end of the third developmental week (Farooq and Dragoi, 2019; Horii-Hayashi et al., 2015; Muessig et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: The early postnatal period described here, where the hippocampus learns the statistics of the body, is a key step for the emergence of self-referenced representations.
source: We would like to propose that the early postnatal period described here, where the hippocampus learns the statistics of the body, and which terminates with the rise of a recurrent inhibitory network, is a key step for the emergence of self-referenced representations onto which exploration of the external world can be grafted.
evidence: This is a proposed interpretation in the Discussion.

claim: An imbalance between self-referenced and environmental hippocampal representations due to a miswiring of local somatic inhibition could have major outcomes and could be on the basis of several neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) and schizophrenia.
source: An imbalance between self-referenced and environmental hippocampal representations due to a miswiring of local somatic inhibition could have major outcomes. It could be on the basis of several neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) and schizophrenia.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal in the Discussion.

claim: Both autism spectrum disorders and schizophrenia have been associated with an aberrant maturation of PV-expressing interneurons.
source: Interestingly, both disorders have been associated with an aberrant maturation of PV-expressing interneurons (Gogolla et al., 2014; Jurgensen and Castillo, 2015; Lewis et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: The proper development of the peripheral sensory system is critically involved in ASD.
source: In addition, the proper development of the peripheral sensory system, which is partly initiating the early CA1 dynamics reported in our study, is also critically involved in ASD (Orefice et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: The period described here corresponds to the third trimester of gestation in humans.
source: The period described here corresponds to the third trimester of gestation and likely extends postnatally given the protracted integration of GABAergic interneurons into functional circuits in the human brain (Murphy et al., 2005; Paredes et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.
